subtitle: Someone else, or you six months from now, can rerun this and get the same result.

code:
a = np.random.default_rng(42).normal(size=3)
b = np.random.default_rng(42).normal(size=3)
c = np.random.default_rng().normal(size=3)
d = np.random.default_rng().normal(size=3)

np.array_equal(a, b)   # True  -- same seed
np.array_equal(c, d)   # False -- unseeded
caption: Same seed, same sequence, every time. The number 42 has no special meaning.

eyebrow: random_state hides inside pandas and scikit-learn
code:
df.sample(n=3, random_state=42)
# order IDs [9, 2, 6] every single run

from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
train, test = train_test_split(df, test_size=0.3, random_state=42)
caption: Set random_state everywhere you split, sample, shuffle, or train a model.
